text:
Jonathan Castagna arrived in Calgary this fall after a 34-point season at Cornell, a third-round pick the Coyotes took in 2023, and he has spent his first 23 NHL games doing the unglamorous work: 12 and a half minutes a night, 48 hits, 20 blocked shots. Then came the night against San Jose when his first two NHL goals carried the Flames, and the headlines started asking whether Calgary had found something.

The goals since are not a fluke. All four of his goals have come in his last ten games, and he's getting better looks while doing it (2.0 expected goals on his own shots, the quality of his chances, against 1.4 usual). He's shooting 19%, above where we'd expect him to settle, so the pace will cool a little.

The bigger question is the minutes. At five on five Calgary is roughly even in shot attempts with him on and a bit behind on chance quality, normal for a rookie in a checking role. If his line starts tilting the ice, he earns more than 12 minutes. That's the thing to watch.
headline: Castagna turns a checking role into goals
